title: Evidence Class Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: xAPI
Learning Analytics
Evidence Classes
Instrumentation
Classification
description: A p5.js sorting activity in which learners assign the interactions of a mock MicroSim (slider, Start/Pause, Reset, diagram node, checked prediction, animation, tab switch) to the seven evidence classes, see the deciding question from the chapter's decision list, and compare the Full-mode statement with the Compact summary fields; a Challenge mode scores eight described events.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Evidence classes and the seven-question decision list
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish the evidence classes by assigning each interaction in a described MicroSim to its class and explaining the deciding question.
prerequisites: The evidence class table and decision list (Chapter 16)

accessibility.notes: Item and Bin dropdowns with an Assign button replace clicking; keys 1-7 choose bins; feedback states correct or not in words as well as color

controls.label: Seven evidence-class bins
controls.purpose: Assign the selected item to a class; hover shows the definition

controls.label: Item
controls.purpose: Keyboard choice of the element to classify

controls.label: Compact mode
controls.purpose: Show the Compact summary fields instead of the Full-mode statement

controls.label: Challenge
controls.purpose: Switch to eight unlabeled events with a score

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided classification with an explicit ordered decision procedure and feedback that names the deciding question
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Select-and-sort with a mode toggle and a scored challenge set
keyQuestions: Which is the first decision-list question that answers yes?
What does Compact mode keep for this interaction, and what does it drop?
Why is an assessment unchanged by the Compact fold?
commonMisconceptions: A button is always a press (a Check button is assessment)
Hovering anything is inspection evidence, whatever its length
Compact mode folds answers into the session summary
assessmentOpportunities: Naming the deciding question for an interaction
Contrasting the Full and Compact records for one item
